details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> ggml: bound views by the bytes their strides reach (#31584) * ggml: bound views by the bytes their strides reach A view was checked against its source with the size of a contiguous tensor of the same shape, computed before its strides were set. Views whose rows overlap failed that check although they stay inside their source, and views with wider strides passed it while reaching past the end. The view functions now pass their strides to the tensor constructor, which checks the bytes they actually reach, like ggml_nbytes. The conv windows of delta_net are created with all their rows at once instead of being widened after the check. * ggml: assert that a strided view starts from contiguous elements The view functions set nb[0] to the type size, so the source must have contiguous elements along dim 0 for the view to read them. </details> **Website:** - <https://llama.app> **Attestations:** - <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/63502997> **macOS/iOS:** - [mac

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: ## Overview This release adds OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization support, a new `flash_attn_ext_rows` op that makes the unified KV cache efficient for multi-sequence inference, and a generic batched tensor copy API. Four new architectures are supported (Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6 and Mistral Large 4), audio generation and transcription expand with Chatterbox TTS, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and predefined Pocket TTS voices, and the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B models get major prefill optimizations. `ggml` is updated to v0.29.0, bringing FP8 E4M3, flash attention rows, NCCL-based multi-node tensor parallelism and performance work across the CPU, CUDA, SYCL, Metal, Vulkan, OpenCL and Hexagon backends. The server and UI receive a round of fixes and refinements. ### Highlights - Quant: OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type (saturating mode) with conversion helpers and a new ftype ([#27512](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27512)) - llama: `flash_attn_ext_rows` - more efficient unified KV for multi-seq, restoring non-u

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> llama : fix on-device state copy sizes for quantized KV caches (#30541) * llama : fix on-device state copy sizes for quantized KV caches The on-device sequence state copies (LLAMA_STATE_SEQ_FLAGS_ON_DEVICE) computed their element count as size / ggml_element_size(). For a quantized type such as q8_0 or q4_0 that is the number of blocks, not elements, so only part of each range was copied: the restored state was wrong, or the copy crashed. Compute the count as size / ggml_type_size() * ggml_blck_size() for the save, the restore and the copy between differently chunked ranges, and assert that each range covers whole blocks. * llama : drop the one-line comments * llama : drop the redundant cast in the state copy size </details> **Website:** - <https://llama.app> **Attestations:** - <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/63869663> **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b12121/llama-b12121-bin-macos-
